title: Zoom in: workers pull only what they have room for
caption: The in-flight limit is the credit: a worker that is slow, for any reason, takes less, and the queue's depth tells everyone upstream.

messages.label: pull up to 5
messages.note: The worker has 5 free slots. It asks for exactly that many: the free slots are its credit.

messages.label: hold seats
messages.note: The DB connection pool (20 per worker host) is the next bound; waiting for a connection times out after 200 ms.

messages.label: ack 5, pull 5 more
messages.note: Acks give the credit back. Throughput = slots ÷ time per order, whatever the arrival rate.

scenarios.name: Payment slows
scenarios.summary: Pull-based workers slow down by themselves: busy slots mean no pulls, and the queue depth carries the signal upstream.

messages.label: ok after 3 s
messages.note: Each slot is now busy 10× longer.

messages.label: no free slots: no pull
messages.note: Nothing is sent upstream; the worker simply stops asking.

messages.label: depth rises → admission sheds
messages.note: The queue's depth is what the API and the waiting room react to.

scenarios.name: Alternative: push
scenarios.summary: If the queue pushes as fast as orders arrive, the worker becomes the unbounded buffer, and a crash loses the lot to redelivery.

messages.label: push 50 more
messages.note: The broker doesn't know the worker is busy.

messages.label: local buffer: 400 orders
messages.note: Memory climbs and every buffered order is aging past its deadline.

messages.label: out of memory: crash
messages.note: Unacked orders are redelivered to the other workers, which are just as overloaded. A prefetch limit turns push back into credit.

scenarios.name: Pool exhausted
scenarios.summary: A bounded connection pool with a short timeout fails fast and frees the slot, instead of piling waiters on a slow database.

messages.label: timeout after 200 ms
messages.note: All 20 connections are busy with slow queries.

messages.label: nack: retry in 5 s
messages.note: The order goes back with a delay and the slot is free again. The database isn't sent more work than it can do.
